newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius steps up sugar plantings in tea areas.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius steps up sugar plantings in tea areas.

text.p: Mauritius has accelerated its programme of switching land under tea into sugar cane, Agriculture Minister Arvin Boolell said on Tuesday.
"The diversification programme has been accelerated and the programme which was initially scheduled for completion in June 1998 is now expected to end by June 1997."

The programme began in February 1995 and aimed to raise sugar production to meet an extra annual export quota of 85,000 tonnes of raw sugar to the European Union which the island obtained under the Special Preferential Sugar (SPS) agreement.

"Out of a total of 5,500 arpents (acres) of the Public Tea Sector earmarked for sugar cane diversification, 4,300 arpents have already been uprooted and 2,000 arpents have been planted; 420 arpents have been harvested this year," Boolell said.
Some 18,000 to 20,000 tonnes of sugar was expected to be produced from land previously under tea cultivation when the programme was completed.

Boolell also cited government measures aimed at encouraging small tea planters to convert to sugar. These included meeting the cost of uprooting tea, loans at concessional rates for the purchase of cane plants and free soil analysis.
Sugar officials see production in Mauritius in a normal season at around 650,000 tonnes.
Production for 1996 has been forecast at 590,000 tonnes because of drought.
In addition to the SPS agreement, Mauritius has an annual export quota of 507,000 tonnes of raw sugar to the European Union under the Sugar Protocol of the Lome Convention.
In 1996, it was also awarded an export quota of 24,000 tonnes to the U.S.
